_about: The operator's model/effort dispatch preferences for /orchestrate. pick-dispatch.mjs asks a classifier which option fits a task brief. Edit freely: options, criteria, tiers, caps and thresholds are all data. Criteria describe what the BRIEF says, never how hard the task will turn out to be — a classifier can only see the text.

judgment-high.criteria: The brief asks for an architecture or design decision where the approach has not been chosen and it lists constraints or trade-offs to weigh; OR it describes a failure that spans several components, concurrency, or intermittent behaviour with no named cause; OR it says an earlier medium-effort attempt failed.

judgment-medium.criteria: The brief asks to review or critique a plan, spec, design document or RFC; OR to diagnose a symptom in one area with no named cause; OR to decide how to handle a security-sensitive change or a data migration; OR to build a new feature or product where the brief states the goal but leaves the approach open.

judgment-low.criteria: The brief asks to review a code change or pull request of any size; OR for a second opinion on a stated decision; OR to answer a question by reading code (find where something happens, explain why).

workhorse-high.criteria: The brief asks to implement a described change or fix, possibly across several files, with a stated goal or acceptance criteria; OR to write tests for existing code.

workhorse-medium.criteria: The brief names both the bug and its fix; OR asks for a change confined to one file or function; OR asks for a document, spec or brief written up from facts and decisions it already states.

workhorse-low.criteria: The brief asks for a rename, a move, or applying a supplied patch or exact spec; OR running a named sequence of commands; OR triage, classification, a summary, or short copy.

ask.criteria: None of the other options fits, or the brief names no artifact and no action.

_evidence: v5 (2026-09-18): implementation routes to workhorse-high, not judgment-low. Blind head-to-head on 5 real merged repo tasks: Opus-high preferred 4/5 by a cross-vendor reviewer (scores 41 vs 37), Fable-low only 6% cheaper and 30% faster; Fable-low stopped early and shipped one incomplete fix. Reviews stay judgment-low (CodeRabbit 2026-09-01: Fable low recall >= high).
